```{=html}
<!-- ── Species modals ── -->
<div class="species-modal" id="sm-greater-glider">
  <div class="species-panel">
    <button class="panel-close" onclick="closeSpecies('greater-glider')">&times;</button>
    <img class="species-panel-img" src="images/species/gl.jpeg" alt="Greater Glider" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.nextElementSibling.style.display='block'"><span class="species-panel-emoji" style="display:none">&#127769;</span>
    <h3>Greater Glider</h3>
    <p class="sci">Petauroides volans</p>
    <span class="taxonomy-badge tx-mammal" style="margin-bottom:.9rem;display:inline-block">Mammal</span>
    <p>The case study species in my 2026 paper — downscaled bioclimatic projections for species distribution modelling in Australia (<em>Environmental Research: Climate</em>, 2026). The Greater Glider is a threatened arboreal marsupial whose range is contracting under warming temperatures; the paper demonstrates how high-resolution climate projections improve SDM accuracy for this species, with implications for conservation planning across its eastern Australian range.</p>
  </div>
</div>

<div class="species-modal" id="sm-ebb">
  <div class="species-panel">
    <button class="panel-close" onclick="closeSpecies('ebb')">&times;</button>
    <img class="species-panel-img" src="images/species/ebb.jpeg" alt="Eastern Bristlebird" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.nextElementSibling.style.display='block'"><span class="species-panel-emoji" style="display:none">&#129413;</span>
    <h3>Eastern Bristlebird</h3>
    <p class="sci">Dasyornis brachypterus</p>
    <span class="taxonomy-badge tx-bird" style="margin-bottom:.9rem;display:inline-block">Bird</span>
    <p>EcoCommons was used to predict undiscovered habitat for this endangered bird — combining known observation records with environmental layers to identify likely undetected populations. Field teams deployed acoustic sensors in the predicted areas and detected new individuals within six months. This outcome was highlighted in the EcoCommons team's 2026 Australian Museum Eureka Prize profile as a demonstration of the platform's real-world conservation impact.</p>
  </div>
</div>

<div class="species-modal" id="sm-noisy-miner">
  <div class="species-panel">
    <button class="panel-close" onclick="closeSpecies('noisy-miner')">&times;</button>
    <img class="species-panel-img" src="images/species/nm.jpeg" alt="Noisy Miner" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.nextElementSibling.style.display='block'"><span class="species-panel-emoji" style="display:none">&#128038;</span>
    <h3>Noisy Miner</h3>
    <p class="sci">Manorina melanocephala</p>
    <span class="taxonomy-badge tx-bird" style="margin-bottom:.9rem;display:inline-block">Bird</span>
    <p>A native honeyeater that has become functionally overabundant in degraded woodland edges, where it aggressively excludes smaller insectivores. The Capertee Valley (NSW) is a key case: Noisy Miner dominance across cleared woodland fragments suppresses Regent Honeyeater recovery by outcompeting them at nectar resources and denning sites — a paradox where a native species becomes a conservation threat. Noisy Miner density was analysed as part of bird community competition assessments, with high densities flagging habitats requiring structural restoration to support functional biodiversity. [Presentation link to follow.]</p>
  </div>
</div>

<div class="species-modal" id="sm-regent-honeyeater">
  <div class="species-panel">
    <button class="panel-close" onclick="closeSpecies('regent-honeyeater')">&times;</button>
    <img class="species-panel-img" src="images/species/rh.jpeg" alt="Regent Honeyeater" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.nextElementSibling.style.display='block'"><span class="species-panel-emoji" style="display:none">&#128330;</span>
    <h3>Regent Honeyeater</h3>
    <p class="sci">Anthochaera phrygia</p>
    <span class="taxonomy-badge tx-bird" style="margin-bottom:.9rem;display:inline-block">Bird</span>
    <p>Critically endangered woodland bird — fewer than 350–500 individuals estimated remaining, making it one of the rarest songbirds in Australia. The Capertee Valley (NSW) holds the largest known population and is central to its recovery, but Noisy Miner competition in degraded woodland edges remains a key pressure alongside habitat loss. The species has also lost song culture in captivity. Use case analysis focused on understanding competition dynamics and priority habitat patches in the Capertee Valley — modelling both the Regent Honeyeater's habitat requirements and Noisy Miner density as a co-occurring pressure layer. [Presentation link to follow.]</p>

<div class="species-modal" id="sm-richmond-birdwing">
  <div class="species-panel">

    <img class="species-panel-img" src="images/species/rbb.jpeg" alt="Richmond Birdwing" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.nextElementSibling.style.display='block'"><span class="species-panel-emoji" style="display:none">&#129419;</span>
    <h3>Richmond Birdwing</h3>
    <p class="sci">Ornithoptera richmondia</p>
    <span class="taxonomy-badge tx-insect" style="margin-bottom:.9rem;display:inline-block">Insect</span>
    <p>One of Australia's largest butterflies, restricted to a narrow corridor of subtropical rainforest in south-east Queensland. The Richmond Birdwing depends on Richmond Birdwing Vine (<em>Pararistolochia praevenosa</em>) as its sole larval host plant — a native climber also restricted to the same range. The invasive Dutchman's Pipe vine (<em>Aristolochia elegans</em>) is a toxic look-alike that lures females to lay eggs on a plant that kills their caterpillars, compounding pressure from host plant decline and habitat fragmentation. Use case work explored the spatial overlap between the butterfly's known range, host plant distribution, and the invasive vine — informing weed management prioritisation and assisted revegetation for host plant recovery. [Presentation link to follow.]</p>

</div>

<div class="species-modal" id="sm-lyrebird">
  <div class="species-panel">
    <button class="panel-close" onclick="closeSpecies('lyrebird')">&times;</button>

    <h3>Superb Lyrebird</h3>
    <p class="sci">Menura novaehollandiae</p>
    <span class="taxonomy-badge tx-bird" style="margin-bottom:.9rem;display:inline-block">Bird</span>
    <p>EcoCommons species distribution models were used to assess the impact of the 2019–20 Black Summer bushfires on Superb Lyrebird and Greater Sooty Owl habitat — estimating what proportion of suitable range was burnt and modelling recovery trajectories across south-eastern Australia. These outputs were cited as key examples of EcoCommons' real-world conservation utility and contributed to the platform's 2026 Eureka Prize win. The lyrebird is also an ecosystem engineer; its scratching and digging cycles nutrients and shapes understorey structure, so its post-fire decline has cascading effects on forest regeneration. A separate research angle explored the nesting relationship between Superb Lyrebirds and Lantana thickets — ground-dwelling birds often utilise dense Lantana as nesting cover in degraded habitats, creating a management paradox: blanket Lantana removal can temporarily eliminate nesting infrastructure before native structural cover regenerates. Assisted revegetation to provide equivalent native ground cover is an important component of restoration design. [Presentation link to follow.]</p>

</div>

<div class="species-modal" id="sm-lantana">

    <h3>Lantana</h3>
    <p class="sci">Lantana camara</p>
    <span class="taxonomy-badge tx-invasive" style="margin-bottom:.9rem;display:inline-block">Invasive</span>
    <p>One of the world's worst invasive plant species — a dense flowering shrub that forms impenetrable thickets, suppresses native understorey, and degrades habitat for ground-dwelling fauna. Distribution data was used alongside native species SDMs to prioritise weed management interventions in subtropical Queensland restoration projects. The management story is ecologically nuanced: Lantana thickets, while destructive at landscape scale, can provide temporary nesting and shelter cover for ground-dwelling birds such as lyrebirds in degraded habitats where native structural cover has been lost. Effective restoration involves targeted Lantana removal paired with assisted revegetation of native shrub equivalents, so ground-nesting species are not left exposed. [Presentation link to follow.]</p>

</div>

    <p>Additional threatened species modelled in separate EcoCommons use case presentations: <strong>Greater Bilby</strong> (<em>Macrotis lagotis</em>), <strong>Armoured Mistfrog</strong> (<em>Litoria lorica</em>), <strong>Northern Hairy-nosed Wombat</strong> (<em>Lasiorhinus krefftii</em>), and <strong>Nangur Spiny Skink</strong> (<em>Nangura spinosa</em>) — all run at QLD scale using MaxEnt, GBM, RF, and ANN algorithms to compare model performance.</p>

<script>
function forceCloseDetailModal(id) {
  const modal = document.getElementById(id);
  if (modal) modal.style.display = 'none';
}

function closeDetailModal(id, event) {
  if (event && event.target && event.target.classList.contains('detail-modal')) {
    forceCloseDetailModal(id);
  }
}

function closeSpecies(id) {
  const modal = document.getElementById('sm-' + id);
  if (modal) modal.classList.remove('open');
}

function initTimelineInteractions(root) {
  const yearButtons = Array.from(root.querySelectorAll('.dneg-year'));
  const yearBlocks = Array.from(root.querySelectorAll('.dneg-year-block'));
  const clickableCards = Array.from(root.querySelectorAll('.dneg-card-clickable'));

  function setActive(year) {
    yearButtons.forEach((button) => {
      button.classList.toggle('is-active', button.textContent.trim() === year);
    });
  }

  yearButtons.forEach((button) => {
    button.addEventListener('click', () => {
      const id = button.dataset.target;
      const target = document.getElementById(id);
      if (target) target.scrollIntoView({ behavior: 'smooth', block: 'start' });
    });
  });

  clickableCards.forEach((card) => {
    const detailId = card.dataset.detail;
    const open = () => {
      const modal = document.getElementById(detailId);
      if (modal) modal.style.display = 'flex';
    };
    card.addEventListener('click', open);
    card.addEventListener('keydown', (event) => {
      if (event.key === 'Enter' || event.key === ' ') {
        event.preventDefault();
        open();
      }
    });
  });

  const observer = new IntersectionObserver(
    (entries) => {
      const visible = entries
        .filter((entry) => entry.isIntersecting)
        .sort((a, b) => b.intersectionRatio - a.intersectionRatio)[0];
      if (visible) setActive(visible.target.dataset.year);
    },
    { threshold: [0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8] }
  );

  yearBlocks.forEach((block) => observer.observe(block));
  if (yearBlocks[0]) setActive(yearBlocks[0].dataset.year);
}

function initGalleryEl(wrapper) {
  const slides = wrapper.querySelector('.gallery-slides, .detail-gallery-slides');
  if (!slides) return;
  const slideEls = Array.from(slides.children);
  if (slideEls.length <= 1) return;
  let current = 0;
  const dots = Array.from(wrapper.querySelectorAll('.gallery-dot'));
  const prev = wrapper.querySelector('.gallery-prev');
  const next = wrapper.querySelector('.gallery-next');
  function goTo(idx) {
    current = ((idx % slideEls.length) + slideEls.length) % slideEls.length;
    slides.style.transform = 'translateX(-' + (current * 100) + '%)';
    dots.forEach((d, i) => d.classList.toggle('is-active', i === current));
  }
  dots.forEach((d, i) => d.addEventListener('click', function(e) { e.stopPropagation(); goTo(i); }));
  if (prev) prev.addEventListener('click', function(e) { e.stopPropagation(); goTo(current - 1); });
  if (next) next.addEventListener('click', function(e) { e.stopPropagation(); goTo(current + 1); });
}

(function () {
  /* ── Dot grids ── */
  document.querySelectorAll('.dot-grid[data-total]').forEach(function(el) {
    var fill = parseInt(el.dataset.fill, 10);
    var total = parseInt(el.dataset.total, 10);
    var overflow = el.dataset.overflow === 'true';
    for (var i = 0; i < total; i++) {
      var d = document.createElement('span');
      d.className = 'dot' + (i < fill ? (overflow ? ' overflow' : ' on') : '');
      el.appendChild(d);
    }
    if (overflow) {
      var plus = document.createElement('span');
      plus.style.cssText = 'font-size:.7rem;font-weight:800;color:var(--accent-deep);align-self:center;margin-left:2px';
      plus.textContent = '+';
      el.appendChild(plus);
    }
  });

  /* ── Tab switching ── */
  const tabButtons = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.tab-btn'));
  const tabPanels = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.tab-panel'));

  function activateTab(name) {
    tabButtons.forEach((button) => button.classList.toggle('is-active', button.dataset.tab === name));
    tabPanels.forEach((panel) => panel.classList.toggle('is-active', panel.dataset.panel === name));
  }

  tabButtons.forEach((button) => {
    button.addEventListener('click', () => activateTab(button.dataset.tab));
  });

  /* ── Sub-tabs (Projects + Imprint) ── */
  document.querySelectorAll('.subtab-btn').forEach((btn) => {
    btn.addEventListener('click', () => {
      const parent = btn.closest('.content-card, .tab-panel');
      const target = btn.dataset.subtab;
      parent.querySelectorAll('.subtab-btn').forEach((b) => b.classList.toggle('is-active', b === btn));
      parent.querySelectorAll('.subtab-panel').forEach((p) => p.classList.toggle('is-active', p.dataset.subpanel === target));
    });
  });

  initTimelineInteractions(document);

  /* ── Gallery init — all timeline cards and detail modals ── */
  document.querySelectorAll('.dneg-media-gallery, .detail-gallery').forEach(initGalleryEl);

  /* ── Species card clicks ── */
  document.querySelectorAll('.species-card').forEach(function(card) {
    card.addEventListener('click', function() {
      var modal = document.getElementById('sm-' + card.dataset.species);
      if (modal) modal.classList.add('open');
    });
  });

  /* ── Click outside to close species modals ── */
  document.querySelectorAll('.species-modal').forEach(function(modal) {
    modal.addEventListener('click', function(e) {
      if (e.target === modal) modal.classList.remove('open');
    });
  });

  /* ── Contact form ── */
  const contactForm = document.getElementById('contact-form');
  if (contactForm) {
    contactForm.addEventListener('submit', (event) => {
      event.preventDefault();

      const name = document.getElementById('contact-name').value || '';
      const email = document.getElementById('contact-email').value || '';
      const subject = document.getElementById('contact-subject').value || 'Website enquiry';
      const message = document.getElementById('contact-message').value || '';

      if (!name.trim() || !email.trim() || !message.trim()) {
        alert('Please complete name, email, and message.');
        return;
      }

      const fullSubject = encodeURIComponent(subject + ' - from ' + name.trim());
      const body = encodeURIComponent(
        'Name: ' + name.trim() + '\n' +
        'Email: ' + email.trim() + '\n\n' +
        message.trim()
      );

      window.location.href = 'mailto:abhirsc@outlook.com?subject=' + fullSubject + '&body=' + body;
    });
  }

  /* ── ESC key ── */
  document.addEventListener('keydown', (event) => {
    if (event.key !== 'Escape') return;
    document.querySelectorAll('.detail-modal').forEach((modal) => {
      modal.style.display = 'none';
    });
    document.querySelectorAll('.species-modal.open').forEach((modal) => {
      modal.classList.remove('open');
    });
  });
})();
</script>
```
